did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens by presenting the song as David’s song of thanksgiving, sung on the day the Lord rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul.
Did you know? David uses several images to describe the Lord’s protection: a rock, a fortress, a refuge, a shield, the horn of salvation, and a stronghold.
Did you know? In his time of distress, David says that he called to the Lord, and the Lord heard his voice and his cry from his temple.
Did you know? The Lord’s response to David’s cry is described in powerful cosmic terms: the earth shakes, and the foundations of the heavens tremble.
Did you know? After describing the storm and the waters, David describes his rescue this way: the Lord reaches down from on high, takes hold of him, and draws him out of deep waters.
Did you know? David connects his rescue with his moral conduct, saying that the Lord rewarded him according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands.
Did you know? David describes divine treatment as corresponding to a person’s conduct: faithful to the faithful, blameless to the blameless, pure to the pure, and shrewd toward the devious.
Did you know? David calls the Lord his lamp and emphasizes that the Lord lights up his darkness and enables him to face dangers and enemies.
Did you know? The song describes the Lord as giving David military skill: He trains his hands for battle and strengthens him even against a powerful bow.
Did you know? At the end of the song, David extends his thanksgiving beyond his personal victories and recalls the Lord’s steadfast love for David and his descendants forever.
